hints.content:
When we have an integral of a sum of functions, we can always split it into the sum of the integrals of each function:

$\displaystyle \int_{0}^5 [g(x)+h(x)] \, dx =\int_{0}^5 g(x) \, dx+\int_{0}^5 h(x) \, dx$

$\displaystyle \int_{0}^5 g(x)\,dx$ is the net area between $y=g(x)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=5$.

![Function g is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 5. The graph consists of a smooth curve. The curve starts at (0, 0), moves upward to a relative maximum in quadrant 1, moves downward and ends at (5, 0). The region below the curve and above the x-axis between x-intercepts 0 and 5 has area 4.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a8c52d22a0b3e18f05073fac5effa71de30c5481)

From the graph:

$\displaystyle\int_{0}^ 5 g(x)\,dx=4$

$\displaystyle \int_{0}^ 5 h(x)\,dx$ is the net area between $y=h(x)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=5$.

![Function h is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 7 to 5. The graph consists of a smooth curve. The curve starts at (0, 0), moves downward to a relative minimum in quadrant 4, moves upward and ends at (5, 0). The region above the curve and below the x-axis between x-intercepts 0 and 5 has area negative 8.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/c17ef7fcbd001b915d54f3cf366be358e4e1e59d)

From the graph:

$\displaystyle\int_{0}^5 h(x)\,dx=-8$

Now we can sum up the two integrals:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\displaystyle \int_{0}^5 [g(x)+h(x)] \, dx
\\\\
&=\displaystyle \int_{0}^5 g(x) \, dx+\int_{0}^5 h(x) \, dx
\\\\
&=4+(-8)
\\\\
&=-4
\end{align}$
